title: Russian troops pull back from Poti and three other positions in western Georgia
body:
On 13 September 2008 Russian soldiers and armoured vehicles pulled back from several positions in western Georgia, meeting a deadline set about a month after the war. Hundreds of troops left earthen-walled bases on the outskirts of the Black Sea port of Poti and at three other western Georgian locations. Georgian Security Council chief Alexander Lomaia said Russia had met its commitment: "They have fulfilled the commitment."

Lomaia said about 250 soldiers and 20 armoured vehicles left, but roughly 1,200 Russian soldiers remained at 19 positions inside Georgia. The Kremlin planned to keep 7,600 soldiers in Abkhazia and South Ossetia, which it had recognised as independent. Russian President Dmitry Medvedev had promised to withdraw from the Poti and buffer-zone posts within 10 days of the deployment of 200 European Union monitors, who were due by 1 October. Georgia, the United States and the EU wanted a full return to pre-war positions, while Russia rejected that and wanted Western monitors kept out of the two regions.

Violence continued. A Georgian policeman was shot dead near the Abkhazia border, with fire reportedly from a Russian-Abkhaz post, and a similar killing occurred three days earlier near South Ossetia. Georgian Deputy Foreign Minister Giga Bokeria said Ossetian paramilitaries burned Georgian homes in Koshka and Disevi; South Ossetian spokeswoman Irina Gagloyeva called the allegation a complete lie. The war had displaced nearly 192,000 people, according to the report.
